summary: Quiet-tenant shadowing leading to granular GPU starvation and p99 throughput regression in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleDocs) reports sudden p99 throughput and latency regression during late-morning traffic window on their dedicated pool. Symptoms show recurring short eviction waves and an atypical sustained p99 rise (~2x) despite nominal GPU allocation. The pool shows a pattern of a low-traffic tenant that intermittently suppresses heartbeats and triggers conservative autoscaler decisions; we are calling this 'quiet-tenant shadowing'.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing degraded user-facing throughput for inference pipelines; p99 latency up from ~320ms to ~760ms for several 15-minute windows.
- Affects production routes pinned to dedicated pool (NimbleDocs production).
- Risk of SLA breach if pattern continues across next 24h window.

Environment:
- Prod dedicated pool: dedicated-us-west-3
- Affected model: gpt-small-optimized-v1 (pinned)
- Autoscaler config: conservative scaling cooldown (5m), slot reservation enabled, predictive window 120s

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Normal traffic includes a mix of long-lived low-CPU/high-GPU streams and short burst streams.
2) During late-morning (~10:20–11:10 PDT), a tenant that sends a few keepalive streams (very low token throughput) begins to suppress heartbeat jitter for ~20–90s sporadically.
3) Scheduler marks slots as less available due to perceived IO_WAIT and reduces batch sizes; autoscaler interprets telemetry drop as decreased demand and triggers micro-shrink decisions.
4) Shrink + fragmented slot allocation causes transient eviction waves as small burst streams attempt to rehydrate KV cache, causing elevated p99 and reduced throughput.

Logs / Observables attached:
- Tail of serving logs showing repeated PAUSE/RESUME events for slot IDs: slot-7b3, slot-8f1 (timestamps 2026-03-10T10:23:14Z -> 2026-03-10T10:30:03Z)
- Autoscaler telemetry: drop in active_streams metric from 120 -> 28 coincident with heartbeat suppression window.
- Traces: increased tail latency prior to eviction spikes; Redis prefetch miss rate increases.

Expected behavior:
Autoscaler should tolerate brief telemetry jitter from very-low-throughput tenants and avoid micro-shrink decisions that cause eviction-induced cache rebuilds. Scheduler should maintain batch fairness and avoid serializing short bursts behind warmup.

2026-03-10 11:20 — SRE (Marco Ruiz): Acknowledged. Collected serving-runtime logs and requested full trace IDs and a top-talkers export from customer's pool. Added to investigation queue.

2026-03-10 12:02 — Customer (NimbleDocs support): Provided request IDs and sampling of traces. Noted that the tenant exhibiting low traffic is their internal monitoring agent (agent-id: nd-agent-03), unfamiliar with causing issues before.

2026-03-10 14:40 — Eng (Priya Desai): Observed repeated short heartbeat gaps (~30–80s) from single tenant stream leading to slot CONTACT_LOST events. Hypothesis: small-stream keepalive pattern interacts poorly with scheduler's slot-health heuristic.

2026-03-11 09:12 — SRE (Marco Ruiz): Implemented temporary mitigation: increased autoscaler cooldown to 8m for affected pool and bumped min_slots by +2 to prevent micro-shrink. Monitoring for 6 hours.
2026-03-12 08:50 — Customer (NimbleDocs support): Reports preliminary improvement in p99 over the morning window; still seeing occasional spikes at ~11:00 PDT.

2026-03-12 12:30 — Eng (Priya Desai): Preparing a targeted scheduler tweak (non-default slot-health smoothing) and a runtime flag to ignore heartbeat gaps from known low-throughput tenants. Planning PR for review.
investigation_notes: Correlated eviction timestamps with heartbeat suppression windows from a single tenant (nd-agent-03). Heartbeat jitter correlates with autoscaler active_streams drop and immediate micro-shrink decisions.
Scheduler's slot-health algorithm currently treats IO_WAIT > 300ms averaged over 30s as slot unhealthy — short keepalive bursts can inflate IO_WAIT without representing sustained load.
KV cache rebuilds after evictions are costly for long-context streams and cause downstream latency for other tenants sharing GPUs; observed prefetch miss rate increase of 18% during events.
Telemetry gap root causes: customer's monitoring agent uses an intermittent long-poll pattern that collided with our heartbeat smoothing window; not a platform network outage.

Tested in staging: simulating quiet-tenant heartbeat jitter reproduces micro-shrink and eviction behavior when autoscaler cooldown <= 5m and min_slots at baseline. Increasing cooldown or min_slots prevents the visible p99 spike.

Related historical tickets and patterns: see SUP-631210 (tenant preemptive eviction) and SUP-51777 (intermittent gpu availability); this appears to be a different surface (heartbeat-suppression-driven decisioning) but shares downstream eviction symptoms.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-11): increased autoscaler cooldown to 8m and raised min_slots +2 for dedicated-us-west-3. Customer p99 improved during monitored windows.

Medium-term fix: engineering to land runtime flag to smooth slot-health calculations for very-low-throughput streams (PR github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5342). This will ignore single-tenant heartbeat gaps under x seconds and avoid treating slots as unhealthy prematurely.

Operational recommendation for customers: identify and tag internal monitoring/keepalive agents as low-priority streams so routing and health heuristics can treat them conservatively; documentation page created on Confluence.

Follow-ups: (1) Add an autoscaler anomaly detector that factors in small-stream signatures before shrinking. (2) Add a targeted dashboard to identify 'quiet-tenant' patterns across dedicated pools. (3) Reach out to NimbleDocs CSM to coordinate a small agent config change to reduce jitter.
Status: patch PR open, staged rollout plan in progress. Temporary mitigations remain active until patch is rolled and evaluated in canary for 48h.
